newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bertelsmann denies aims to buy McGraw-Hill.
newsitem.headline: Bertelsmann denies aims to buy McGraw-Hill.

text.p: German media giant Bertelsmann AG has no plans to buy U.S. publisher McGraw-Hill Inc, a Bertelsmann spokesman said, denying a report in Friday's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung.
But the spokesman said he could not comment on a Wall Street Journal report that Bertelsmann would add cash to its partner America Online's bid for rival Compuserve.
Bertelsmann denies aims to buy McGraw-Hill
Of the McGraw-Hill report, the spokesman said, "There is nothing in that."

The Wall Street Journal said Bertelsmann is adding cash to America Online Inc's offer to buy rival CompuServe Corp Inc. AOL's bid of about $1 billion in stock has so far been rejected by H&R Block Inc, which owns 80 percent of Compuserve.
Bertelsmann operates AOL's service in Germany, and also packages AOL software in some of its music CDs.
AOL, which has about 8.5 million customers worldwide, is interested in Compuserve to pick up its three million customers, add to its corporate clients, and expand its network capacity.
